_comment: The sections of design-decisions.md that count toward a Secure by Design checklist control, read the way security-notes.json's are (crates/sv-check/src/notes.rs): a section with an answer and a `Written by:` line makes its control *documented* (the owner's, once recorded through `sv review`) or *stated by the AI coding tool*, never *checked*. The design-time prompts in design-prompts.json write these headings, without an id, so each section names the heading it goes by (`heading`), and a test holds each to the words its prompt uses. `notCovered` is said beside the credit: what the control asks that a written section cannot show. The file's other sections ("When to bring in a person", "Safe defaults") count toward no control and are read in crates/sv-check/src/decisions.rs. SBD-MT-05 (records kept current) is not here: whether a decision was re-read before a change is not something a file shows. The owner's decisions of 5 October 2026 (BACKLOG, design-time item 9).

sections.title: What we do if something goes wrong
sections.heading: What we do if something goes wrong
sections.asks: What is the plan when something goes wrong: how to take the app offline, what to do if a key leaks, what to do if someone else's data may have been seen, and who to ask for help?
sections.notCovered: Whether the plan has been rehearsed, and whether it would work, is not covered: a written plan is all a file can show.

sections.title: Rules that might apply
sections.heading: Rules that might apply
sections.asks: Which laws or industry rules might apply to this app, from what it keeps and who uses it, and what each would mean for the design?
sections.notCovered: Whether the design really follows those rules is not covered: that takes a person who knows them.
